title: Nuclear Medicine and Clinical PET/CT Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional Non-Standard; not described here as ACGME-accredited fellowship)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Advanced post-residency physician self-study; mirrors programme expectation of completed diagnostic radiology or NM residency. Not for replacing medical school or residency.
recommendedPreparation: Medical anatomy, physiology, pathology and clinical terminology
Introductory imaging physics and diagnostic imaging
Awareness that patient care and radionuclide use require local licensed, supervised teams
prerequisites.requiredTrainingNotice: This course does not determine Hopkins admission or ABNM/ABR pathway equivalence.

objectives: Select and explain imaging modality/tracer reasoning for a clinical question.
Interpret core PET/CT and SPECT concepts using biodistribution, anatomy and artifact checks.
Distinguish observation from inference and write a qualified report.
Explain safety, pediatric optimization, radiopharmacy and therapy concepts without unauthorized procedural instruction.
Use published ABNM blueprint domains as a learning map and date-check clinical sources.
Respect case-image access, deidentification and reuse conditions.

units.title: Clinical NM workflow, patient safety and board frame
objectives: Distinguish the named JHU non-standard fellowship from accredited NM residency and board eligibility.
Apply the ABNM published broad domain map without treating it as a pass predictor.
Frame an indication, modality rationale and concise qualified report.
topics: Clinical question→tracer→instrument; appropriateness; history, screening, limitations, communication, tumor board.
Appropriateness and referral data sufficiency; separate observed examination facts from inference, missing context and management decisions.
units.casePractice: Use linked IAEA case to draft an indication and report skeleton; do not copy image.
units.assessment: 5-point rubric: indication, history/limits, modality rationale, qualified conclusion, safety/communication.

units.title: Radiation physics, detectors and hybrid image formation
objectives: Explain PET coincidence and SPECT collimation clinically.
Trace attenuation, scatter, randoms, reconstruction and CT correction to interpretation.
Identify alignment/reconstruction artifacts.
topics: Decay, detection, gamma camera, count statistics, attenuation correction, resolution, PET/CT registration.
CT purpose (attenuation/localization versus diagnostic) and PET/CT registration; QC and reconstruction effects on apparent uptake and cross-study comparability.
units.casePractice: Annotate artifact type and clinical consequence on IAEA linked gallery, link-only.
units.assessment: Artifact station: mechanism, manifestation, consequence, verification.

units.title: Protocols, radiopharmacy, quantitation and radiation protection
objectives: Relate indication and patient factors to acquisition principles.
Explain radiopharmacy/QC and biologic uptake variation.
Apply radiation protection concepts and escalate under local rules.
topics: Radiopharmacy, preparation, uptake time, glucose/motion, SUV caveats, CT dose, pregnancy/lactation, contamination.
Quality systems, preparation context, contamination escalation and jurisdictional authorization boundaries; this syllabus supplies no activity prescription or unsupervised procedure.
units.casePractice: Fictional protocol deviation case: identify missing info and escalation, never prescribe activity.
units.assessment: Safety memo: hazards, process/escalation, relevance (5 points).

units.title: SPECT/CT and general NM patterns
objectives: Choose conceptual roles for SPECT/CT localization.
Build differential with biodistribution and cross-sectional correlation.
Flag historical practice needing current review.
topics: Bone, infection, renal, endocrine, pediatric SPECT; localization; false positives; image fusion.
Separate normal distribution and localization from disease inference; document anatomic correlation, false-positive alternatives and historical versus current practice.
units.casePractice: Compare IAEA case with current reference; flag obsolete tracer/practice.
units.assessment: Oral-style finding, differential, limitation, needed evidence.

units.title: FDG PET/CT oncology, biodistribution and incidental findings
objectives: Describe physiologic FDG biodistribution and benign uptake.
Integrate PET and CT without equating uptake and diagnosis.
Reason about staging/restaging, inflammatory and treatment confounds.
topics: Preparation; benign variants; brown fat/muscle; infection; incidental findings; staging and reporting.
Read FDG uptake as a context-dependent observation; document CT role, prior examinations, technical comparability and inflammatory or treatment-related alternatives.
units.casePractice: IAEA gallery: compare normal, benign incidental, malignant and non-FDG examples.
units.assessment: Three reports scored for pattern, alternatives, staging language, incidental findings, citation.

units.title: PET response assessment and lymphoma
objectives: Differentiate baseline staging and response question.
Use criteria only in validated context and document comparability.
Calibrate response synopsis to evidence.
topics: Lymphoma response, treatment effects, timing, serial comparisons, partial-volume limits.
For serial lymphoma studies, verify subtype, baseline images, therapy interval, acquisition comparability and applicability of Lugano/Deauville before assigning a formal response category.
units.casePractice: Read IAEA examples longitudinally; distinguish observation from clinical inference.
units.assessment: Response synopsis scored for comparison, framework, limitation, calibration.

units.title: PSMA PET selection, interpretation and reporting
objectives: Describe guideline routine clinical scenarios.
Recognize ligand-specific distribution and false-negative micrometastatic limits.
Produce structured qualified report.
topics: Initial staging; recurrence; persistent disease; nmCRPC; RLT selection; E-PSMA/PROMISE context; pitfalls.

Separate PSMA ligand-specific distribution, physiologic ganglionic/urinary activity, target heterogeneity, microscopic-disease limits, structured reporting and current label-specific patient selection.
units.casePractice: Use IAEA non-FDG cases and guideline tables; no image copying.
units.assessment: Report rubric: question, distribution, limitation, differential, calibrated conclusion.

units.title: Theranostics and radiopharmaceutical therapy
objectives: Explain theranostic pairing and multidisciplinary selection.
Check label/guideline rather than generalize indications.
Recognize marrow, renal, radiation safety risks.
topics: 177Lu-PSMA, PRRT, radioiodine, Ra-223 concepts, dosimetry, treatment response and safety.

Distinguish theranostic concept, therapy-imaging selection, current jurisdiction-specific indication, safety evaluation, release planning and authorized treatment; older recordings are historical supplements only.
units.casePractice: Fictional tumor board: identify missing eligibility/label facts; no treatment order/dose.
units.assessment: Therapy memo: indication/date, imaging selection, risk, follow-up (5 points).

units.title: Cardiac PET and nuclear cardiology
objectives: Integrate perfusion and gated function.
Identify alignment, motion, bolus, myocardial creep errors.
Interpret flow reserve with confounders.
topics: Perfusion, gated function, stress, flow/MFR, attenuation correction, artifacts, amyloid domain.
Report tracer/model, quality, rest and stress myocardial blood flow, flow reserve, gated data and CT role together; do not interpret a reserve ratio without its components and context.
units.casePractice: Use source guideline quality checklist then interpret hypothetical case.
units.assessment: Readout scored for perfusion, LV function, technical quality, caveat.

units.title: Neuro-PET, infection/inflammation and multisystem imaging
objectives: Compare disease-specific tracer biology and question.
Distinguish physiologic, inflammatory, treatment and malignant activity.
State PET cannot establish etiology alone.
topics: Neurodegeneration, sarcoidosis, infection, FUO, vasculitis, false positives, correlation.
Brain FDG pattern interpretation requires preparation, medications, movement, attenuation-correction and clinical differential review; infection/inflammation uptake is not etiologic proof.
units.casePractice: Select related IAEA cases/webinars and make alternatives matrix.
units.assessment: Differential matrix: tracer, pattern, competitors, limitation, evidence.

units.title: Pediatric NM and radiation protection
objectives: Explain pediatric optimization priorities.
Do not transfer adult acquisition defaults casually.
Describe pregnancy/lactation screening and escalation.
topics: Age/size principles, pediatric oncology, communication, radiation safety; no patient dose calculation.

Use age/size-appropriate justification and individualized coverage, caregiver preparation, optimization and local safety protocols; do not transfer adult defaults or calculate patient activity in this course.
units.casePractice: Use linked pediatric IAEA material; draft risk/benefit communication note.
units.assessment: Protocol critique: indication, optimization, safety, communication.

units.title: Integrated readout, quality, research and exam synthesis
objectives: Produce source-grounded report across cases.
Communicate unexpected findings, quality and uncertainty.
Map review to ABNM domains without claiming readiness.
topics: Tumor board, research methods, source currency, ethics, all exam domains and quality.
Integrate a qualified report with source date, evidence/inference distinction, image rights, privacy and quality limitations; link to authentic source examples instead of copying them.
units.casePractice: Capstone using linked IAEA gallery and lawful TCIA subset; no image rehost.
units.assessment: Rubric: accuracy 25%, differential 20%, safety 20%, report 15%, citations 10%, ethics 10%.

assignment.title: Source-grounded PET/CT case conference dossier
deliverables: Select two IAEA linked cases/gallery examples or one authorized TCIA defaced CC BY case and one IAEA link. No image copied without verified permission.
For each: clinical question, tracer/distribution, finding, correlation, differential, quality limits and qualified impression.
Create one-page fictional board-style conference note with dated source, three citations and fact/inference/unknown distinctions.
Add an ethics/access note; for TCIA cite Gatidis & Kuestner (2022), DOI 10.7937/gkr0-xv29.
assignment.passStandard: Formative 80/100 only; not clinical competence or board readiness.

assessment.format: Nine original MCQ, unit assignments, case portfolio and capstone. No protected board questions.
assessment.feedback: Provide explanations and source links; refresh time-sensitive content.
assessment.limitations: Not validated, no human review, board affiliation or passing prediction; cannot assess clinical care or procedures.

unitMap.text: Clinical NM workflow, patient safety and board frame
coveredTopics: Clinical question→tracer→instrument; appropriateness; history, screening, limitations, communication, tumor board.
Appropriateness and referral data sufficiency; separate observed examination facts from inference, missing context and management decisions.

unitMap.text: Radiation physics, detectors and hybrid image formation
coveredTopics: Decay, detection, gamma camera, count statistics, attenuation correction, resolution, PET/CT registration.
CT purpose (attenuation/localization versus diagnostic) and PET/CT registration; QC and reconstruction effects on apparent uptake and cross-study comparability.

unitMap.text: Protocols, radiopharmacy, quantitation and radiation protection
coveredTopics: Radiopharmacy, preparation, uptake time, glucose/motion, SUV caveats, CT dose, pregnancy/lactation, contamination.
Quality systems, preparation context, contamination escalation and jurisdictional authorization boundaries; this syllabus supplies no activity prescription or unsupervised procedure.

unitMap.text: SPECT/CT and general NM patterns
coveredTopics: Bone, infection, renal, endocrine, pediatric SPECT; localization; false positives; image fusion.
Separate normal distribution and localization from disease inference; document anatomic correlation, false-positive alternatives and historical versus current practice.

unitMap.text: FDG PET/CT oncology, biodistribution and incidental findings
coveredTopics: Preparation; benign variants; brown fat/muscle; infection; incidental findings; staging and reporting.
Read FDG uptake as a context-dependent observation; document CT role, prior examinations, technical comparability and inflammatory or treatment-related alternatives.

unitMap.text: PET response assessment and lymphoma
coveredTopics: Lymphoma response, treatment effects, timing, serial comparisons, partial-volume limits.
For serial lymphoma studies, verify subtype, baseline images, therapy interval, acquisition comparability and applicability of Lugano/Deauville before assigning a formal response category.

unitMap.text: PSMA PET selection, interpretation and reporting
coveredTopics: Initial staging; recurrence; persistent disease; nmCRPC; RLT selection; E-PSMA/PROMISE context; pitfalls.

Separate PSMA ligand-specific distribution, physiologic ganglionic/urinary activity, target heterogeneity, microscopic-disease limits, structured reporting and current label-specific patient selection.

unitMap.text: Theranostics and radiopharmaceutical therapy
coveredTopics: 177Lu-PSMA, PRRT, radioiodine, Ra-223 concepts, dosimetry, treatment response and safety.

Distinguish theranostic concept, therapy-imaging selection, current jurisdiction-specific indication, safety evaluation, release planning and authorized treatment; older recordings are historical supplements only.

unitMap.text: Cardiac PET and nuclear cardiology
coveredTopics: Perfusion, gated function, stress, flow/MFR, attenuation correction, artifacts, amyloid domain.
Report tracer/model, quality, rest and stress myocardial blood flow, flow reserve, gated data and CT role together; do not interpret a reserve ratio without its components and context.

unitMap.text: Neuro-PET, infection/inflammation and multisystem imaging
coveredTopics: Neurodegeneration, sarcoidosis, infection, FUO, vasculitis, false positives, correlation.
Brain FDG pattern interpretation requires preparation, medications, movement, attenuation-correction and clinical differential review; infection/inflammation uptake is not etiologic proof.

unitMap.text: Pediatric NM and radiation protection
coveredTopics: Age/size principles, pediatric oncology, communication, radiation safety; no patient dose calculation.

Use age/size-appropriate justification and individualized coverage, caregiver preparation, optimization and local safety protocols; do not transfer adult defaults or calculate patient activity in this course.

unitMap.text: Integrated readout, quality, research and exam synthesis
coveredTopics: Tumor board, research methods, source currency, ethics, all exam domains and quality.
Integrate a qualified report with source date, evidence/inference distinction, image rights, privacy and quality limitations; link to authentic source examples instead of copying them.

topicGaps: 2.310773 verified specialty-specific hours, 2.461944 foundation hours, and 4.772718 total target-counted external hours; 31.227282 hours remain to the 36-hour video target.

Verified specialty recordings are concentrated in prostate PSMA PET/theranostics; no verified full-length clinical lecture was established for broad SPECT/CT interpretation, lymphoma response, myocardial PET, neuro-PET, infection/inflammation, pediatric clinical imaging, or contemporary radiopharmaceutical therapy safety.
The original packet’s generic 61-minute clip targets and five authored episodes are scripts/plans only. Neither target minutes nor scripted narration count as recorded/rendered hours.

Public IAEA webinar listings disclose clinically relevant candidates, but some direct YouTube metadata requests were blocked with HTTP 403/429 and two legacy SNMMI players returned 404; these remain uncounted until public playback and runtime can be verified.
Human clinical review has not been performed. The residual gap is real; no evidence supports padding it with unrelated physics, repeated PSMA material, or unmeasured original production.

practiceQuestions.stem: A hybrid scan is misregistered. What is safest interpretation?

options.text: PET/CT localization helps, but alignment and attenuation artifacts remain possible.
Focal activity proves malignancy.
CT makes PET redundant.
Fusion eliminates motion.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Review both datasets and registration; fused images do not prove histology or eliminate artifact.

practiceQuestions.stem: An FDG focus has insufficient history and no comparison. What next?

options.text: Call metastasis.
Obtain indication, treatment timing, prior images and anatomic correlate before qualifying interpretation.
Ignore all uptake.
Recommend therapy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDG is not tumor-specific; context, timing and correlation distinguish plausible physiologic, inflammatory and malignant causes.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does a negative PSMA PET imply about microscopic pelvic nodes?

options.text: Excludes them.
Cannot exclude them due to PET sensitivity limitations.
Proves no PSMA expression anywhere.
Rules out biochemical recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guideline notes a negative PSMA scan cannot exclude microscopic nodal disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which uses does the joint PSMA guideline list as routine?

options.text: Initial staging, recurrence/persistence, nmCRPC localization and staging before PSMA RLT.
Universal cancer screening.
Only primary diagnosis.
Only postoperative response.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are the routine use cases in the 2023 procedure guideline; other scenarios are potential applications.

practiceQuestions.stem: FDA 2025 expanded Pluvicto indication?

options.text: Any painful bone metastases.
Adults with PSMA+ mCRPC treated with ARPI and appropriate to delay taxane chemotherapy; select using approved PSMA PET.
All hormone-sensitive disease.
Only after all therapies.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA notice date 2025-03-28 defines expanded use and PSMA PET selection.

practiceQuestions.stem: FDA identifies which Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan risks?

options.text: Radiation exposure, myelosuppression, renal toxicity.
Only nausea.
No radiation risk.
Only contrast allergy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are listed in FDA notice; real use requires current label/qualified teams.

practiceQuestions.stem: What can confound cardiac PET flow assessment?

options.text: CT attenuation misalignment, motion or myocardial creep.
The 17-segment model.
Qualitative perfusion interpretation.
Comparing rest and stress.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The open guideline describes misalignment, motion, bolus and myocardial creep pitfalls.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which principle is appropriate for a pediatric NM referral?

options.text: Adult defaults always.
Pediatric optimization, local qualified supervision; this course does not set patient activity.
Skip safety screening.
Shorten acquisition without quality review.

practiceQuestions.rationale: IAEA provides pediatric optimization and protection guidance; this independent course is not a dosing authority.

practiceQuestions.stem: Does this self-study establish ABNM/ABR eligibility?

options.text: Yes.
No: board-specific training, supervised experience, licensure and exams still govern; the course confers none.
Any PET course confers same board.
Hopkins non-standard fellowship guarantees both.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABNM and ABR rules are separate and training-dependent; Hopkins names its fellowship non-standard.

title: PET/CT Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics Fellowship
level: Supplementary physician clinical fellowship self-study course; not a residency or a board-qualifying programme-aligned independent study

prerequisites.audience: Postgraduate physician learners who have completed radiology or nuclear medicine residency, or advanced learners using this strictly for contextual study; not intended to confer competence.
requiredKnowledge: oncology and common clinical laboratory concepts
ability to read scientific/clinical guidelines critically
prerequisites.accessibility: Independent self-study, openly linked readings wherever possible; no rotations, patient care, supervised scanning or therapy, credentialing, or access to Emory confidential curriculum.

objectives: Describe PET radiopharmaceutical target-binding and radiotracer limitations.

Apply radiation safety awareness without claiming handling authorization.
Use structured, calibrated reporting with differential diagnoses, uncertainty and source traceability.
Distinguish the Emory PET/CT fellowship from separately listed nuclear radiology and nuclear medicine residency training and board certification pathways.

topicGaps: The verified public-recording ledger totals 7.5861 h; the exact gap to the 36-hour floor is 28.4139 h. No target/planned minutes, textbooks, conference schedules or authored scripts count as rendered video.

PET physics, instrumentation, PET/CT QC and general tracer development now have accessible verified viewing, but these general/foundation recordings do not amount to full contemporary clinical teaching in FDG tumour interpretation, indication-specific acquisition, inflammatory/physiologic mimics, or structured response assessment.

Public verified clinical recordings remain thin for PSMA tracer-specific interpretation and pitfalls, SSTR/NET grading and dual-tracer reasoning, post-2026 product-specific therapy selection, and integrated reporting. The Medality lecture is a single broad expert overview; accessible account/course add-ons are excluded.

No counted public full-length teaching was verified for local radiation-safety rules/authorized-user eligibility, pregnancy/lactation workflow, treatment-specific organ toxicity surveillance, or complete patient-specific dosimetry. IAEA dosimetry and two broken/unverified PET QC links are retained only as uncounted source-gap candidates.

Emory describes three weekly didactic conferences, clinical PET, protected research, and imaging/physics/radiochemistry teaching, but publishes neither an open syllabus nor recordings/runtimes; no private course content is inferred.

The floor is a video-hours target only. The course is supplementary self-study and does not substitute for supervised clinical training, board eligibility, licensure, authorized-user status or treatment/procedure authorization.

medical.trackType: Supplementary physician clinical fellowship self-study course; not a residency or a board-qualifying programme
boardNames: American Board of Nuclear Medicine (ABNM) initial certification examination — separate physician board pathway; Emory PET/CT applicants must already be ABNM board-eligible or board-certified (depending on route).

American Board of Radiology (ABR) Diagnostic Radiology certification and Nuclear Radiology subspecialty examination — distinct board pathways; this Emory PET/CT fellowship alone is not documented as the required ACGME/RCPSC training for ABR subspecialty certification.
medical.boardStatus: The Emory PET/CT Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics Fellowship is a clinical-research fellowship, not a specialty residency. Emory separately lists a Nuclear Medicine Residency and a Nuclear Radiology Fellowship. ABNM offers a separate Nuclear Medicine certification examination; ABR offers a separate Nuclear Radiology Subspecialty Exam. There is no separate PET/CT Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics board exam identified by Emory, ABNM or ABR in the official sources reviewed.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Emory states PET/CT fellowship applicants must have completed a nuclear medicine or radiology residency and be ABNM or ABR board eligible/certified, plus be eligible for unrestricted Georgia licensure. Completing this PET/CT fellowship does not itself confer ABNM/ABR eligibility, subspecialty certification, Georgia licensure, or NRC authorized-user status. ABNM and ABR eligibility is determined by the respective boards and accredited training requirements; verify individually.

officialProgrammes.name: PET/CT Fellowship (Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page (read 2026-10-07) describes two one-year combined clinical-research fellowships, clinical PET, protected/research time, research requirement, multiple hospital settings, three weekly didactic conferences including clinical nuclear medicine, physics/computer techniques/radiochemistry, and applicant prerequisites including nuclear medicine or radiology residency plus ABNM/ABR board-eligible or certified status. It does not publish a detailed syllabus, a complete lecture inventory, accredited status, or an official number of didactic video hours. This packet treats it as a genuine physician clinical fellowship but explicitly supplementary to residency/board eligibility.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One supplied institutional programme variant only: Emory University School of Medicine’s PET/CT Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics Fellowship. It is not combined with Emory Nuclear Radiology Fellowship, Emory Nuclear Medicine Residency, generic ABNM/ABR board domains, a radiologic technologist programme, or medical physics education. These distinct Emory physician offerings are listed as separate pages; their content is not silently equated. No Harvard or Johns Hopkins variant is asserted for this Emory-specific programme.
sourceCaveats: Programme page can change and does not disclose its full internal lecture/case curriculum; no Emory lecture recording set was assumed or reproduced.
ACGME requirements page points to requirements effective 2026-07-01, but no assertion is made that this PET/CT fellowship is itself ACGME-accredited.

ABNM certification eligibility requires qualifying residency and other board-specific conditions. ABR nuclear radiology exam requires separate prerequisites; neither eligibility nor pass is guaranteed by this course.

FDA Pluvicto page reflects a July 31, 2026 approval as of content current Aug 3, 2026; 2022 label link is an older snapshot. The current full label was not independently retrieved here. Lutathera label PDF is 2024 and warns it may not be latest. Date-check before any clinical use.
No real patient case, image or record was copied. Case references are linked resources; licensing and privacy conditions apply.

Human clinical review has not been performed. Self-study does not substitute for medical education, accredited clinical training, supervised patient care/procedures, institution radiation-safety requirements, licensure, board eligibility or certification.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes what a theranostic pair establishes?

options.text: A diagnostic tracer proves that therapeutic uptake will be uniform in every tumor deposit.
A diagnostic ligand can demonstrate target-associated distribution relevant to therapy selection, but heterogeneity and modality-specific limitations remain.
All tracers for one molecular target have identical biodistribution and accuracy.
A positive PET scan alone authorizes radionuclide therapy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The PSMA guideline describes target expression assessment and explicitly notes radioligand-specific biodistribution and interpretive pitfalls; positive target imaging supports selection but is not, alone, treatment authorization.

practiceQuestions.stem: A serial SUV comparison is most defensible when which condition is met?

options.text: Scan preparation, uptake time, acquisition, reconstruction, calibration and measurement conditions are sufficiently standardized and documented.
Both scans have SUVmax reported, regardless of protocol.
Only the same scanner manufacturer is used.
The lesion is larger than 5 mm, so partial-volume effects do not matter.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Quantitative comparison depends on acquisition and reconstruction standardization and multiple measurement factors. A shared SUV metric alone does not ensure comparability.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an explicit routine clinical use in the joint PSMA PET guideline?

options.text: Routine screening of asymptomatic average-risk adults.
Pre-radioligand-therapy staging of prostate cancer.
Replacing prostate biopsy in all suspected cases.
Definitive exclusion of prostate cancer by a negative scan.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The joint guideline lists staging before PSMA-directed radioligand therapy as routine use and does not make a PET scan a universal substitute for histopathology or clinical judgment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which pitfall is most appropriate to consider when interpreting PSMA-ligand PET?

options.text: All PSMA radioligands have identical physiologic distribution.
Benign/physiologic uptake and tracer-specific biodistribution can mimic or obscure disease; correlate with anatomy and context.
Any focal skeletal uptake is metastatic prostate cancer.
A negative lesion proves it is PSMA-negative at histology.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline notes differing biodistribution and common interpretive pitfalls among PSMA ligands. Imaging findings require contextual interpretation; uptake does not provide histologic proof.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with a well-differentiated GEP neuroendocrine tumor is being evaluated for receptor imaging. Which statement best fits the SSTR PET standard?

options.text: SSTR PET is never used before PRRT.
SSTR PET is commonly used for staging and selection for PRRT, while tumor differentiation and receptor expression affect modality choice.
SSTR avidity proves a tumor is low grade.
FDG PET is prohibited in neuroendocrine neoplasms.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The SSTR PET guideline lists initial staging and selection for PRRT among common indications, describes grade/differentiation and notes FDG may be more useful in some higher-grade/poorly differentiated disease.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the FDA-listed July 31, 2026 Pluvicto approval context on the cited page?

options.text: Monotherapy for all localized prostate cancer.
In combination with ARPI therapy for adults with PSMA-positive metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive prostate cancer, with selection using an approved PSMA PET product.
Therapy for all patients with elevated PSA regardless of imaging.
A screening indication in men without cancer.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The FDA page dated August 3, 2026 reports the July 31, 2026 approval and states the indicated context and PSMA PET-based selection. Label details and later changes must be checked before clinical use.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the safest interpretation of the 2022 Pluvicto PDF available at the cited FDA URL?

options.text: It is necessarily the latest label in October 2026.
It is a dated label snapshot and should not be used alone to determine current indications; consult current FDA label and dated approval notices.
It supersedes all later FDA notices.
It is an ABNM exam blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The source itself says to visit FDA for current labeling; the subsequent FDA notice dated 2026 confirms an approval after the 2022 label.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is accurate about the Emory PET/CT Molecular Imaging and Theragnostics Fellowship?

options.text: It is a physician residency that by itself confers ABNM eligibility.

It is an explicitly one-year combined clinical-research fellowship described by Emory; applicants must already have completed nuclear medicine or radiology residency and be ABNM/ABR board eligible or certified.
It is a technologist certificate course.
It has a separate PET/CT specialty board examination.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory describes two one-year combined clinical-research fellowships and states eligibility requirements including prior residency and ABNM or ABR status. It does not identify an independent PET/CT board exam.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes Emory’s PET/CT fellowship from its nuclear radiology fellowship?

options.text: They are the same offering with interchangeable titles.

Emory lists distinct pages: the PET/CT fellowship requires prior nuclear medicine or radiology residency and board eligibility/certification, while nuclear radiology is a separate fellowship with its own eligibility description.
The PET/CT fellowship is the Emory Nuclear Medicine residency.
The labels on Emory’s pages imply that all graduates are automatically dual certified.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official pages separately list PET/CT fellowship, nuclear radiology fellowship, and nuclear medicine residency. Certification or eligibility depends on board and accredited training rules, not labels alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the right use of a publicly accessible TCIA collection in this course?

options.text: Copy selected images into the course without attribution because they are de-identified.
Link learners to the selected collection, check its dataset-specific license/terms, do not attempt re-identification, and cite its DOI if actually used.
Assume every collection has identical CC BY 4.0 terms.
Download patient records and upload them into assignments.

practiceQuestions.rationale: TCIA data are de-identified but collection licenses vary; its policy prohibits efforts to identify participants, requires dataset attribution and cautions against mirroring.

topicGaps: The deduplicated ledger now has 5.066944 observed hours against the 36-hour target; 30.933056 hours remain. Of these, 0.919722 hours are adult/congenital supplementary context rather than pediatric-specialty teaching, leaving 31.852778 specialty hours to the target if only specialty-specific recordings are credited.

Recordings now add congenital TEE, 3D echo, pediatric congenital CT/MR case review, congenital CT and general CHD-imager background. These are individual webinars/lectures, not a complete advanced fellowship course.

No evidence was found for 36 freely accessible hours of pediatric cardiac-imaging recordings. The current verified ledger and scripted original episodes do not close that floor; scripts are not videos and planned target minutes are not hours delivered.

Topic-level recording gaps remain in lesion-specific pediatric CMR acquisition and hemodynamics, fetal echo beyond a short uncounted overview, complete systematic pediatric TTE practice, intraoperative imaging, rare lesions and current supervised image interpretation.

The CT/MR primer and congenital CT webinar support conceptual comparison only. They do not provide institutional pediatric safety protocols, dose authorization, contrast protocols, or supervised image acquisition.

Public institutional fellowship pages describe modalities, broad rotations and prerequisites but do not disclose full didactic syllabi, actual lecture-session contents, patient volumes, procedure/case numbers, or validated assessment rubrics.

Additional discovered fetal-echo media remain uncounted where the full runtime or direct playback could not be established; one ASE360 overview page is publicly accessible but its full player runtime was not observed.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Advanced clinical physician fellowship (senior cardiac-imaging training; not a separate board specialty). Boston Children’s GME directory marks its track Non-ACGME; JHACH page does not state accreditation status.

medical.boardStatus: No separate U.S. pediatric cardiac-imaging specialty board examination identified in reviewed ABP/ABMS sources. ABP Pediatric Cardiology subspecialty certification is the relevant physician board pathway; this fellowship itself is not that certifying pathway.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: The ABP currently requires three years of full-time broad-based pediatric cardiology fellowship in an ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited program, verification of training/scholarly activity, and passing the subspecialty exam. Neither this course nor an advanced imaging fellowship alone confers eligibility. Check ABP current rules.

officialProgrammes.institution: Boston Children’s Hospital / Harvard Medical School teaching hospital
officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Cardiac Imaging Senior Fellowship (official page also calls it Advanced Cardiac Imaging Fellowship)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes 2–3 fellows/year, comprehensive TTE/TEE/intraoperative/fetal echo, CMR and CT; approximately 80% clinical and 20% research; clinical time relatively evenly divided among modalities; didactics and conferences. Applicant on track to complete categorical pediatric cardiology fellowship or equivalent international training. Boston Children’s GME directory lists it among senior fellowships; packet records accreditation “No”/Non-ACGME.

officialProgrammes.name: Pediatric Advanced Cardiac Imaging Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Distinct exact variant: year-long programme, one fellow/year; 3-week boot camp, 42-week advanced imaging, 3-week general cardiology inpatient service and 20 vacation days; 40% pediatric echo, 20% research, and remaining 40% fetal echo and CT/MRI divided according to interest. Requires completed ACGME-accredited Pediatric Cardiology fellowship. Page does not state this programme’s accreditation classification; status left unspecified.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet names Boston Children’s; public official research additionally verified Johns Hopkins All Children’s Hospital (JHACH), a separate institution and distinct curriculum, so both exact variants are preserved. Do not conflate JHACH with the Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore. Institutional pages are programme descriptions, not independent evidence of accreditation or ABP certification eligibility. Boston Children’s catalogue differentiates its three-year categorical Pediatric Cardiology fellowship from senior fellowships.
sourceCaveats: Sources checked 2026-10-07. Official pages are subject to change; confirm current programme, board rules, and guidance before relying on details.
BCH packet says its listing’s accreditation field is No. JHACH page gives no accreditation status; do not infer one.

No separate U.S. pediatric cardiac imaging board exam was identified in the reviewed sources; ABP Pediatric Cardiology certification is the related board pathway. This is a bounded source review, not a universal assertion about every voluntary certificate.
ABP certification eligibility is governed by ABP and requires accredited pediatric cardiology training; completing any course or imaging fellowship does not guarantee eligibility.
Clinical human review not performed. This independent self-study resource has no Harvard/JHU affiliation and is not accredited clinical training.
No diagnosis/case volume, eligibility beyond what official pages state, guaranteed passing, procedural competence, licensure or certification is claimed.
Rights and access restrictions are reported; free-to-view does not mean permission to copy or redistribute.
The ABP outline used is labeled effective Oct 1, 2022; subsequent updates should be checked before use.
All patient-like examples and practice questions are fictional; no actual patient record or image is embedded.

topicGaps: The deduplicated ledger now has 5.066944 observed hours against the 36-hour target; 30.933056 hours remain. Of these, 0.919722 hours are adult/congenital supplementary context rather than pediatric-specialty teaching, leaving 31.852778 specialty hours to the target if only specialty-specific recordings are credited.

Recordings now add congenital TEE, 3D echo, pediatric congenital CT/MR case review, congenital CT and general CHD-imager background. These are individual webinars/lectures, not a complete advanced fellowship course.

No evidence was found for 36 freely accessible hours of pediatric cardiac-imaging recordings. The current verified ledger and scripted original episodes do not close that floor; scripts are not videos and planned target minutes are not hours delivered.

Topic-level recording gaps remain in lesion-specific pediatric CMR acquisition and hemodynamics, fetal echo beyond a short uncounted overview, complete systematic pediatric TTE practice, intraoperative imaging, rare lesions and current supervised image interpretation.

The CT/MR primer and congenital CT webinar support conceptual comparison only. They do not provide institutional pediatric safety protocols, dose authorization, contrast protocols, or supervised image acquisition.

Public institutional fellowship pages describe modalities, broad rotations and prerequisites but do not disclose full didactic syllabi, actual lecture-session contents, patient volumes, procedure/case numbers, or validated assessment rubrics.

Additional discovered fetal-echo media remain uncounted where the full runtime or direct playback could not be established; one ASE360 overview page is publicly accessible but its full player runtime was not observed.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A pediatric TTE checklist is missing pulmonary venous connections. Which interpretation is most defensible?

options.text: Normal pulmonary venous anatomy is established because no abnormality was noted.
The study has a limitation; document it and consider whether additional views or another modality are needed for the clinical question.
The missing views prove TAPVR.
CT is required in every case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Absence of documented visualization is not proof of normal anatomy; ASE recommends systematic assessment of pulmonary veins, with cross-sectional imaging when needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educational question asks which board certifies pediatric cardiology in the United States. Which is correct?

options.text: ABR pediatric cardiac imaging board
ABP pediatric cardiology subspecialty certification
ACGME cardiac imaging board
ASE pediatric imaging board

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABP administers pediatric cardiology subspecialty certification after required accredited fellowship training; ACGME accredits programs, not individuals. No separate US pediatric cardiac imaging board exam was identified.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the clearest reason not to infer pulmonary venous obstruction from a limited TTE alone?

options.text: TTE can never evaluate pulmonary veins.
Incomplete visualization creates uncertainty; Doppler and complementary TEE/CT/CMR may be needed based on context.
Only MRI detects pulmonary veins.
All pulmonary venous Doppler is diagnostic.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASE describes TTE as primary but notes other modalities may be used for diagnostic confirmation; absence of adequate visualization must be reported.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a fictional congenital follow-up question about ventricular volumes and flow, which modality is especially suited to provide non-ionizing volumetric and flow assessment?

options.text: CMR
Plain chest radiograph
A single ECG lead
No imaging

practiceQuestions.rationale: CMR includes cine ventricular volumetry and phase-contrast flow approaches described in the SCMR congenital consensus; protocol and safety are individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is a sound principle when considering pediatric cardiac CT?

options.text: Use CT for all follow-up because it is fastest.
Choose the protocol for a specific question and minimize radiation consistent with diagnostic need.
CT has no ionizing radiation.
Use the same adult settings for every child.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pediatric CT planning is individualized; radiation optimization is an explicit concern.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fetal screening study is abnormal. What is the appropriate conceptual next step in this educational framework?

options.text: Treat the screening finding as definitive anatomy.
Diagnostic fetal echocardiography can confirm and refine anatomy, with communication and limitations made explicit.
Wait until birth in all cases.
Use Doppler without regard to safety guidance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASE fetal recommendations distinguish screening and diagnostic fetal echocardiography and describe a systematic comprehensive examination.

practiceQuestions.stem: A researcher asks to put EchoNet-Peds clips into this course webpage. What does its posted research-use agreement permit?

options.text: Anyone may redistribute all files.
Free noncommercial research use with restrictions; no distribution/reproduction absent permission and no clinical reliance.
Commercial hosting is allowed.
Permission to view automatically grants republication rights.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Stanford states research-only, noncommercial permission and prohibits redistribution/reproduction without specific prior written permission; it is not for patient-care reliance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A TTE report lists one normal window but omits other required segments due to poor cooperation. Best documentation?

options.text: State the study is wholly normal.
Report the visualized findings, name limitations and state what remains unevaluated.
Delete the report.
Assume normal anatomy from age.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A comprehensive examination includes required elements; explicit technical limitations preserve the distinction between not seen and normal.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about advanced cardiac imaging senior fellowship eligibility is most accurate for Boston Children’s official page?

options.text: Applicants need only a high-school science course.
Applicants should be on track to complete categorical pediatric cardiology fellowship or equivalent international training before entry.
It is a substitute for pediatric cardiology residency.
Completion guarantees board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Boston Children’s describes the prerequisite and does not suggest the imaging fellowship replaces core training or guarantees a board credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a posted fellowship curriculum from board eligibility?

options.text: One year of senior imaging fellowship automatically qualifies a learner for ABP subspecialty certification.
ABP certification requires three years of full-time accredited pediatric cardiology fellowship plus other criteria; senior imaging fellowship is a different training track.
Any online course substitutes for accredited fellowship.
A hospital directory is the board examination blueprint.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABP requirements specify three years of accredited pediatric cardiology fellowship and a passing certifying exam; program listings and board blueprints are distinct.

title: Pediatric Imaging Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (independent educational supplement; not a training program)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: For intended advanced learners: completed medical degree and diagnostic radiology residency (or equivalent physician-level radiology preparation); this course cannot validate credentials.
Working knowledge of radiographic, fluoroscopic, ultrasound, CT, MRI and nuclear-medicine principles; pediatric physiology and developmental anatomy; contrast and radiation-safety basics.
Ability to interpret imaging in supervised practice is not implied. Learners without physician training should use this as general educational material only and not make clinical decisions.
objectives: Select and justify pediatric imaging tests and protocols using the clinical question, age, modality strengths, appropriateness guidance, radiation minimization and sedation/safety context.

Distinguish normal developmental anatomy and common variants from urgent pathology across fetal, neonatal, infant, child and adolescent imaging, while stating uncertainty and a differential when appropriate.
Develop systematic, modality-aware interpretations across the ABR study guide's broad chest/cardiac/face/ENT/airway; MSK/spine/CNS; and GI/GU/interventional domains.
Communicate time-critical findings, recommend proportionate next steps, and collaborate with pediatric clinical teams, technologists, physicists and caregivers.
Explain limitations of public case libraries, privacy and image licensing; use only authentic de-identified linked cases within source terms; never rehost patient images or records.
Use original formative questions and structured case review to identify knowledge gaps; these assessments are not validated predictors of ABR performance.

units.title: Developmental anatomy, approach and consultation
objectives: Use age, gestational age, clinical context and question to structure an interpretation.
Separate expected developmental appearances from variants and findings needing follow-up.
Communicate limitations and urgency without overcalling.
topics: Fetal-to-adolescent anatomy; normal maturation; structured search patterns; comparison; clinical consultation
boardDomains: ABR general pediatric radiology; congenital anomalies and variants; cross-domain interpretation
ACGME milestones: consultant; interpretation; basic and clinical science
units.casePractice: Choose one freely viewable Radiopaedia pediatric case; inspect source-reported age/context and images on the source site; write an observation-first differential. Do not download, repost or assume a single example is representative.
units.assessment: Submit a structured report with age-appropriate normal variants, top differential, uncertainty, and one clinically relevant recommendation; rubric: observation accuracy 40%, age/context 20%, differential 20%, clear communication 20%.

units.title: Pediatric imaging selection, protocols and radiation safety
objectives: Compare modality risks, benefits and protocol tradeoffs for child-specific questions.
Apply justification and optimization principles; recognize that dose should be tailored to patient and task.
Identify sedation, contrast, preparation and communication considerations requiring local protocols.
topics: ALARA/optimization; size- and question-adapted CT; ultrasound/MRI first considerations when appropriate; dose metrics; contrast safety; sedation coordination
boardDomains: ACGME milestones: protocol selection and optimization; consultant
ABR cross-cutting modalities and image quality
units.casePractice: Use a public ACR pediatric appropriateness scenario; compare the selected test with one alternative and cite a current local protocol source before applying in practice.
units.assessment: One-page modality-selection memo. Rubric: clinical question 25%, appropriateness evidence 25%, risk/benefit 25%, explicit local-policy caveat 25%.

units.title: Chest, airway and neonatal thoracic imaging
objectives: Use age and support devices to approach neonatal and pediatric chest imaging.
Describe airway, lung, pleural, mediastinal and line/tube findings systematically.
Escalate an immediately consequential finding using institutional communication pathways.
topics: Neonatal lung disease; pneumonia; airway; chest wall; devices; congenital thoracic lesions; pediatric chest tumors
boardDomains: ABR: Chest, cardiac, facial bones/ENT/airway; neonate and infant
units.casePractice: Review linked public neonatal chest cases on Radiopaedia without copying images; compare image observations with a cited open lecture and state the limits of single-view assessment.
units.assessment: Create a device-and-lung checklist and interpret two linked public cases. Rubric: systematic coverage 30%, device localization 25%, differential 25%, escalation/reporting 20%.

units.title: Pediatric cardiovascular and fetal imaging
objectives: Describe a segmental approach to congenital cardiovascular anatomy.
Identify what CT, MRI, ultrasound and radiography each contribute to a defined question.
Explain how prenatal findings inform—but do not replace—postnatal imaging and clinical evaluation.
topics: Congenital heart disease; cardiac CT/MR; vascular rings; fetal brain/body MRI; prenatal/postnatal correlation
boardDomains: ABR: Chest and cardiovascular; congenital anomalies and variants
units.casePractice: Use a linked fetal or congenital cardiac case from a public case library and cite the exact page; do not infer clinical outcome beyond information on that page.
units.assessment: Draw an unlabeled segmental map and propose a modality sequence for a fictional referral. Rubric: anatomic logic 40%, modality rationale 30%, uncertainty/collaboration 30%.

units.title: Neuroimaging, neonatal brain and pediatric emergencies
objectives: Use age-appropriate modality selection in common neurologic presentations.
Recognize emergent patterns and differentiate urgent observation from causal inference.
Apply structured reporting and communication for findings requiring prompt action.
topics: Neonatal brain sonography; brain/skull; infection, seizure, trauma, tumor, developmental anomalies; spine
boardDomains: ABR: CNS, spine, congenital anomalies, infection, neoplasm and trauma
units.casePractice: Use the ACR criteria and public cases to discuss a fictional emergency question; distinguish imaging observations from clinical diagnosis and consult local pathways.
units.assessment: Case conference note with modality justification and communication plan. Rubric: appropriateness 30%, differential 30%, urgency 20%, limits/communication 20%.

units.title: Gastrointestinal imaging and acute abdomen
objectives: Structure a pediatric abdominal interpretation by age, site and likely mechanism.
Describe the complementary roles of radiography, ultrasound, fluoroscopy, CT and MRI.
Avoid assuming a single imaging sign proves a diagnosis; state key differential and next step.
topics: Neonatal obstruction; vomiting; abdominal emergencies; bowel inflammation/infection; abdominal trauma; solid organs
boardDomains: ABR: Esophagus/stomach, small bowel, colon, liver, spleen, pancreas; trauma and other
units.casePractice: Read a linked public pediatric abdominal case and compare it to a current ACR scenario; record the modality-specific positive and negative observations.
units.assessment: Submit a 5-step imaging reasoning note for a fictional vomiting case. Rubric: question formulation 20%, modality choice 25%, systematic findings 30%, differential/limits 25%.

units.title: Genitourinary, fetal urinary tract and pelvic imaging
objectives: Approach common pediatric GU questions with ultrasound-first reasoning where appropriate and current guidance.
Describe postnatal follow-up questions after a prenatally detected finding without assuming a fixed protocol.
Recognize that classification and follow-up depend on system-specific standards and clinical context.
topics: Renal/urinary tract dilatation; congenital urinary anomalies; renal/adrenal masses; scrotal ultrasound; reproductive anomalies
boardDomains: ABR: Kidney, ureter, bladder, urethra, genital and adrenal
units.casePractice: Use a linked public pediatric GU case and applicable current ACR topic; do not copy images or convert a teaching case into a patient-management plan.
units.assessment: Write an age/context-based modality memo and annotated differential. Rubric: relevant context 20%, modality choice 30%, observations 30%, safety/limits 20%.

units.title: Musculoskeletal, spine and developmental bone
objectives: Recognize age-related skeletal appearance and common developmental variants.
Construct a focused differential for pain, injury, infection, tumor and metabolic disease.
Apply a systematic trauma approach and communicate potential safeguarding concerns objectively.
topics: Bone maturation; trauma; skeletal dysplasia; metabolic bone disease; infection; bone and soft-tissue tumors; sports/overuse
boardDomains: ABR: MSK/spine, congenital, infection, neoplasm, trauma, metabolic/endocrine/toxic, dysplasia
units.casePractice: Review linked public skeletal cases with source attribution; distinguish pattern recognition from proof of mechanism or intent.
units.assessment: Structured skeletal survey interpretation exercise using an authorized case source. Rubric: completeness 30%, age-appropriate pattern 25%, differential 25%, neutral documentation 20%.

units.title: Pediatric oncology, masses and vascular anomalies
objectives: Use age, compartment and organ of origin to organize pediatric mass differentials.
Describe staging/extent questions that affect imaging choices and interdisciplinary care.
State uncertainty and avoid treatment recommendations outside imaging scope.
topics: Chest/abdominal/renal/adrenal masses; bone and soft-tissue tumors; CNS neoplasms; vascular anomalies; follow-up imaging
boardDomains: ABR: Neoplasm across chest, CNS, MSK and GI/GU; vascular/interventional
units.casePractice: Use public linked cases and record source differential and age context; do not download or re-host the clinical images.
units.assessment: Tumor-board style fictional imaging summary. Rubric: location/extent 30%, differential 25%, relevant next-imaging question 25%, multidisciplinary communication 20%.

units.title: Pediatric trauma, non-accidental injury and child protection
objectives: Describe imaging findings objectively and recognize when pattern/context mismatch merits further evaluation.
Separate radiologic observation from causal attribution; apply current institutional safeguarding procedures.
Explain modality choice and radiation considerations in trauma.
topics: Head and skeletal trauma; accidental and inflicted injury differential; documentation; multidisciplinary communication; uncertainty
boardDomains: ABR: MSK/CNS trauma; chest/abdomen trauma; consultant and communication
units.casePractice: Use only a linked, authentic, de-identified teaching case whose source makes it publicly available. No copying/redistribution; use neutral observations and applicable institutional policy.
units.assessment: Write a structured observation and escalation note for a fictional scenario. Rubric: accurate description 35%, differential 25%, neutral non-causal language 20%, appropriate escalation 20%.

units.title: Pediatric intervention, nuclear medicine and multidisciplinary practice
objectives: Describe the role and limits of image-guided procedures and pediatric nuclear/molecular imaging.
Identify preparation, consent, radiation-protection and escalation needs; do not perform procedures from course material.
Communicate across the care team and distinguish radiology fellowship scope from a separate subspecialty track.
topics: Vascular access and image-guided procedures; nuclear medicine/PET; pediatric thyroid/MIBG services as institution-specific; team-based practice; complications and safety
boardDomains: ABR: Vascular and interventional; cross-modality; consultant/procedural competency domains
units.casePractice: Discuss a linked public case using source-defined context; no procedure planning, dose instruction or unsupervised intervention is provided.
units.assessment: Interdisciplinary handoff simulation based on fictional facts. Rubric: question 25%, safety/escalation 35%, role boundaries 20%, concise communication 20%.

units.title: Quality, research literacy, reporting and board-style synthesis
objectives: Use evidence-based imaging criteria while checking current versions and limits.
Appraise the difference between a fellowship curriculum, ACGME requirements/milestones and a board study outline.
Construct a concise differential and answer original formative questions with evidence-linked reasoning.
topics: Quality/safety; image optimization; evidence appraisal; audit and scholarly project concepts; reporting; board-style integration and remediation
boardDomains: ABR published study guide domains (general outline, not exhaustive); ACGME milestones: quality improvement, practice-based learning, professionalism and communication
units.casePractice: Use public linked cases only. For each, distinguish source-reported facts, observations, inference and unknowns; do not treat a case archive as prevalence data.
units.assessment: Cumulative original 10-item formative quiz plus case memo; rubric: accuracy 40%, rationale 25%, source/date awareness 15%, communication 20%. Not validated board prediction.

assignment.title: Pediatric imaging consult portfolio
assignment.instructions: Complete one fictional case memo per unit using public case links only; include clinical question, developmental context, modality/protocol rationale, observations, prioritized differential, uncertainty, communication and source attribution. Do not make real-patient decisions, copy images or patient records, or claim procedural competency.
assignment.completionThreshold: Self-study formative threshold 80% on rubric; no certificate of clinical competence or board readiness is conferred.

assessment.method: Formative original practice set (10 items), twelve case/interpretation memos and one final synthesis. Self-score with answer rationales; remediate missed concepts against dated official guidance. No clinical skills examination or supervised observation is included.
assessment.limitations: Questions are original educational items, not official ABR questions, psychometrically validated items, or a validated predictor of passing. No guaranteed passing or board eligibility.

studyHours.status: study plan, not observed training time
studyHours.plan: 12 units x approximately 10 learner-hours each (public lecture viewing where available, readings, case review and assignment); this 120-hour estimate is a learner workload plan only. It is not the official fellowship didactic/clinical hour total, cannot replace supervised fellowship rotations, and is not counted as video hours.

topicGaps: Observed accessible recording ledger totals 15.11556 h (14.49361 specialty + 0.62194 foundation), leaving 20.88444 h to the 36 h all-recording target. The 36 h floor is not achieved; scripted episodes/plans do not count as video hours.

Observed additions improve pediatric CNS, fetal MRI, MSK injury, pediatric hepatic tumor, and renal mass coverage. They remain discrete lectures rather than a comprehensive or current curriculum in those subjects.

Substantial topic/media gaps remain: broad fetal body imaging and congenital cardiac imaging; face/ENT/airway; complete neonatal and pediatric CNS (including age-specific normal development, spine, infection, trauma and neoplasm); comprehensive chest and abdominal organ/interventional topics; scrotal/reproductive/GU anomalies and follow-up; pediatric nuclear medicine; interventional practice; image optimization/contrast/sedation teamwork; quality improvement, research literacy and communication. The public AAR catalogue names several of these lectures but did not expose directly observable runtimes in this task, so they remain uncounted.

The ABR study guide remains a coarse, dated (its PDF says last verified 2017), explicitly non-exhaustive outline. ACGME milestones are formative and only intended for use in accredited programs. Public recordings do not confer clinical competence, ABR eligibility, or supervised fellowship experience.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The packet's Emory offering is verified. Emory and Children's Healthcare of Atlanta describe one collaborative ACGME-accredited pediatric radiology fellowship. This is a clinical physician fellowship, not a residency, combined specialty program, research-only postdoc or generic directory category. Pediatric neuroradiology and pediatric interventional radiology are adjacent but separately named tracks and excluded. No Harvard or Johns Hopkins variant is asserted for this assigned Emory packet. ACGME accreditation is a program status, not this self-study course's accreditation.
sourceCaveats: This assigned track is Emory/Children's, not a claim that every Harvard-affiliated or Johns Hopkins clinical programme is covered by this single specialty file.
The ABR study-guide PDF is accessible from a 2025 path but its own text says last verified June 19, 2017; treat it only as a coarse exam-domain outline and verify current exam resources with ABR.

The ABR publicly describes Pediatric Radiology subspecialty certification and an exam, so a separate subspecialty exam exists; there is not a separate primary-board specialty exam. Eligibility is not conferred here.

The ACR clinical pathway and SPR resource portal expose dynamic material. The SPR educational resources page states free non-member access requires creation of a free account/log-in; those content items are not counted as free public videos and login-only materials are not used.

No human clinical review was performed. An independent educational course is not affiliated with Emory, Children's, ACR, ACGME or ABR and provides no accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, procedure competence, or certification.

topicGaps: Observed accessible recording ledger totals 15.11556 h (14.49361 specialty + 0.62194 foundation), leaving 20.88444 h to the 36 h all-recording target. The 36 h floor is not achieved; scripted episodes/plans do not count as video hours.

Observed additions improve pediatric CNS, fetal MRI, MSK injury, pediatric hepatic tumor, and renal mass coverage. They remain discrete lectures rather than a comprehensive or current curriculum in those subjects.

Substantial topic/media gaps remain: broad fetal body imaging and congenital cardiac imaging; face/ENT/airway; complete neonatal and pediatric CNS (including age-specific normal development, spine, infection, trauma and neoplasm); comprehensive chest and abdominal organ/interventional topics; scrotal/reproductive/GU anomalies and follow-up; pediatric nuclear medicine; interventional practice; image optimization/contrast/sedation teamwork; quality improvement, research literacy and communication. The public AAR catalogue names several of these lectures but did not expose directly observable runtimes in this task, so they remain uncounted.

The ABR study guide remains a coarse, dated (its PDF says last verified 2017), explicitly non-exhaustive outline. ACGME milestones are formative and only intended for use in accredited programs. Public recordings do not confer clinical competence, ABR eligibility, or supervised fellowship experience.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner reviewing an infant study is unsure whether a structure is abnormal or reflects maturation. What is the most defensible first step?

options.text: Apply adult anatomy expectations because the modality is the same.
Establish age and clinical context, then compare the observation with age-appropriate anatomy and current reference guidance.
Label the finding as congenital without further context.
Ignore developmental anatomy when image quality is adequate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pediatric interpretation depends on developmental stage and context; observation should precede inference. ACGME milestones explicitly include infant/child/adolescent imaging anatomy and normal-versus-abnormal interpretation. This is a learning principle, not a diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: A request does not make the clinical question clear. Which action best reflects a pediatric radiology consultant role?

options.text: Proceed with the highest-radiation study to maximize detail.
Clarify the question and relevant information with the clinical team, then consult current evidence-based criteria and local protocol.
Choose a modality based only on what the service uses most often.
Decline every ambiguous referral without discussion.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME milestones describe clarification of clinical question, relevant data gathering and use of evidence-based guidance. The particular imaging choice remains scenario-specific.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes pediatric CT dose optimization?

options.text: Use adult settings in all children to preserve comparability.
Use a justified examination and tailor optimization to the patient and diagnostic task under current institutional protocols.
Avoid all CT, regardless of urgency or modality alternatives.
A course lecture authorizes a learner to set clinical protocols independently.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Image Gently emphasizes child-focused imaging safety, and protocol selection/optimization is a supervised ACGME competency. The question intentionally avoids prescriptive dose values; actual protocols require local expert governance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A public case page contains a useful pediatric image. What is the safest course-material practice?

options.text: Download and place the image in the course because it is publicly viewable.
Link to the source case and follow its terms; do not reproduce unless the exact license permits this use and attribution.
Remove the creator's name and upload the image.
Assume all online clinical images are public domain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Radiopaedia states case material is generally CC BY-NC-SA with attribution and share-alike requirements, and public viewing is not blanket rehosting permission. This course links rather than copies clinical images.
practiceQuestions.domain: Privacy, image rights and educational integrity

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees a pediatric chest image with a potentially critical finding. Which next step is most appropriate in this educational framework?

options.text: Wait until the next routine report queue without checking urgency.
Describe the finding accurately and communicate through the institution's time-critical reporting pathway.
Infer cause from the image alone and bypass the clinical team.
Send the image through personal messaging to a peer.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME milestones include recognition of critical reportable findings, consultation and communication. The correct local method depends on institutional policy; this course does not authorize real-world interpretation.
practiceQuestions.domain: Chest imaging, critical findings and communication

practiceQuestions.stem: A newborn with vomiting is being discussed in a fictional teaching case. Which statement is best supported?

options.text: One ultrasound observation alone proves the cause.
Imaging observations such as bowel dilation or wall changes must be interpreted with clinical context and modality limits; consult current local guidance.
All newborns with vomiting need the same modality sequence.
No imaging question needs clarification if the symptom is common.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The open review describes sonographic findings that may be seen in neonatal bowel obstruction, but findings require contextual interpretation and do not themselves establish a specific diagnosis or universal test sequence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which resource is the best starting point for checking evidence-based imaging appropriateness for a defined pediatric scenario?

options.text: A dated, broad exam outline alone.
The current relevant ACR Appropriateness Criteria topic, considered with local policy and the clinical team.
Anecdotal preference from a single case.
A public lecture title with no associated guidance.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR describes its criteria as evidence-based guidance for appropriate imaging/treatment decisions. The ABR study guide itself is a non-exhaustive general outline and its PDF says last verified 2017.

practiceQuestions.stem: A source-linked fictional trauma case has findings that raise concern for inflicted injury. What wording best preserves scientific and professional limits?

options.text: State a causal conclusion from imaging alone.
Document objective observations, give a differential, and follow local safeguarding/clinical escalation pathways.
Omit the finding to avoid interpretation.
Publish the case image to ask the public.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A structured radiology description should distinguish observation from causal attribution and be managed through current institutional safeguarding pathways. The CDC source is background information, not a stand-alone imaging standard.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is accurate about Emory/Children's pediatric radiology training and this course?

options.text: This course includes supervised rotations at the listed hospitals.
The institutional program describes a one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship with broad rotations; this independent course does not provide those clinical experiences.
The fellowship is a research-only postdoctoral job.
A self-study course awards ACGME accreditation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Emory and CHOA publicly describe one-year ACGME-accredited clinical physician fellowship training and rotations. The independent curriculum is unaffiliated and offers neither supervised training nor accreditation.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does the ABR Pediatric Radiology credential represent?

options.text: A separate primary physician board unrelated to diagnostic radiology.
An ABR subspecialty certification/examination with eligibility prerequisites; this course neither confers eligibility nor certification.
An automatic credential for any viewer of a pediatric radiology lecture.
A guarantee of successful examination if a learner watches 36 hours.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABR identifies Pediatric Radiology as a subspecialty examination with training/certificate and other eligibility requirements. The course cannot establish any prerequisite or guarantee an outcome.

assignment.title: Integrated pediatric neuroimaging case conference (educational simulation)
assignment.instructions: Select a lawfully accessible, de-identified teaching case from the linked public repositories, or clearly label a constructed vignette as fictional. Submit a structured image-description worksheet, age/context statement, modality/protocol rationale, two- to four-item ranked differential, urgent communication point if relevant, uncertainty/limitations statement, source citations and a 5-minute oral case presentation. Do not copy or rehost any clinical images, reports, or patient records.
assignment.rubric: 12 points: clinical question/age/timing (0–2); localization and sequence-specific observations (0–2); differential supported by pattern (0–2); modality/protocol reasoning and safety (0–2); urgency, communication and limitations (0–2); lawful sourcing and citations (0–2). Suggested formative threshold 10/12 only; not validated, board-predictive or credentialing.

assessment.format: 12 unit case worksheets; 10 original single-best-answer knowledge questions; one integrated educational case assignment.
assessment.rubric: Formative only. For case work score age/context, localization, observations, reasoning, communication/safety, uncertainty and sourcing. Questions include answer rationales and source links. No proprietary or leaked exam questions used. No predictive validity or passing guarantee.

unitMap.text: Pediatric neuroradiology scope, age, and systematic approach
coveredTopics: Age-dependent anatomy and myelination; modality selection; structured report; communication and escalation.

unitMap.text: Fetal and congenital brain development
coveredTopics: Fetal MRI; cortical development; callosal anomalies; posterior fossa; neural tube defects; syndromic context.

unitMap.text: Neonatal brain: maturation, prematurity, and hypoxic-ischemic injury
coveredTopics: Prematurity; germinal matrix/intraventricular hemorrhage; white-matter injury; term HIE; neonatal seizures; therapeutic hypothermia context.

unitMap.text: Pediatric trauma and suspected abusive head trauma
coveredTopics: PECARN context; acute CT; subacute/chronic MRI; abusive head trauma as a distinct pathway; spinal injury; non-accidental injury differential.

unitMap.text: Epilepsy, cortical dysplasia, and neurocutaneous disorders
coveredTopics: Epilepsy protocol; focal cortical dysplasia; hippocampal development; tuberous sclerosis and phakomatoses; presurgical localization limits.

unitMap.text: Pediatric brain tumors and treatment response
coveredTopics: Posterior fossa; supratentorial; sellar/suprasellar; embryonal/glial tumors; staging; response and treatment effects.

unitMap.text: Infection, inflammation, demyelination, and immune-mediated disease
coveredTopics: Meningitis/ventriculitis; abscess; encephalitis; demyelination; autoimmune/inflammatory patterns; immunocompromised host.

unitMap.text: Pediatric cerebrovascular and vascular malformations
coveredTopics: Arterial ischemic stroke; hemorrhage; venous thrombosis; arteriovenous malformations; vasculopathy; vascular imaging.

unitMap.text: Pediatric spine and spinal cord
coveredTopics: Dysraphism; tethering; tumors; myelitis; infection; trauma; degenerative and post-operative findings.

unitMap.text: Head, neck, orbit, skull base, and temporal bone
coveredTopics: Orbits; craniofacial development; sinonasal disease; temporal bone; skull base; neck spaces; cranial neuropathies.

unitMap.text: Metabolic, genetic, and neurodegenerative patterns
coveredTopics: Leukodystrophies; metabolic/toxic injury; basal ganglia; neurodegeneration; mitochondrial patterns; skeletal-neuro syndromes.

unitMap.text: Quality, safety, protocoling, and integrated case reasoning
coveredTopics: Dose awareness; sedation coordination; contrast/safety screening; peer learning; discrepancy communication; case synthesis.

topicGaps: The 36.000-hour verified-video target remains unmet: 1 unique accessible specialty recording contributes 1.0911 observed hours (65:28); 34.9089 hours (34:54:32) remain. Scripted episodes and clip-plan target minutes are not rendered video and contribute zero hours.

Only units 1, 2, 5, 9 and 11 have the newly verified lecture mapped; units 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 12 have no verified external lecture from this expansion. The single recording is a broad introductory lecture, not comprehensive coverage of mapped units.

No publicly playable 36-hour institutional pediatric neuroradiology lecture archive was verified. ASPNR lists 31 free lectures, but the recording link leads to its member/e-learning area; login-free recording access and durations could not be established, so none counted.

Important insufficiently recorded domains remain: neonatal maturation and injury; trauma and separate suspected-abuse pathway; brain tumor protocols and response; infection/inflammation; cerebrovascular emergencies; detailed pediatric spine and cord; head-and-neck/orbit; metabolic/genetic patterns; protocol/safety/quality; age-specific normal development.

Five complete original teaching scripts are authored and source-mapped, but they are scripted only, not rendered or uploaded. Their content, nor the existing pilot or planned clip minutes, is not included in verified hours.

36 verified hours are not currently feasible from the verified public recording set. Closing the 34.9089-hour gap requires discovery and validation of additional unique open recordings or substantial original recording/production; this work does not establish feasibility or promise that source-backed material can fill the gap.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.
